requirement: Describe the study as a prospective multisite three-arm randomized parallel trial comparing PNS plus PT, PNS plus sham PT, and sham PNS plus PT, with four weeks of treatment and follow-up through Week 28.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the three randomized treatment combinations, concurrent four-week PNS/PT period and outcomes visits through Week 28.
The analysis attachment compares the same three groups over treatment and follow-up.

requirement: Implement the protocol's adaptive treatment assignment to minimize imbalance across the three groups on baseline BPI-SF3 pain above versus at most 6, pain duration at least versus below 18 months, age at least versus below 55 years, and study site; document the allocation probabilities, seed and concealment procedure before use.

evidence.text: The protocol names an adaptive minimization algorithm and the four balancing variables but does not give implementation details.

requirement: State masking by role without a blanket label: reconcile the protocol's double-blind description and blinded face-to-face outcome assessment with the registry's participant, care-provider and outcome-assessor masking, and specify which implant staff and physical therapists can infer active versus sham treatment.

evidence.text: The protocol calls the study double blinded, describes sham procedures and states that outcomes are administered face-to-face in a blinded manner, but does not fully map masking by role.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 96 randomized participants, 32 per group, obtained by inflating the 27-per-group statistical requirement by an anticipated 20% dropout rate; do not substitute the registry's later actual enrollment of 96 as independent sample-size evidence.

evidence.text: The protocol records a 96-participant target and says 96 participants will be randomized.
The analysis attachment derives 27 per group and inflates to 32 per group, total 96, for 20% dropout.

requirement: Define the primary analysis population operationally, including whether all randomized participants are analyzed as assigned, whether lead implantation or any treatment exposure is required, and how ineligible randomizations, absent baseline values, treatment discontinuation, lead replacement and prohibited shoulder therapy are handled.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomization, treatment, follow-up, lead replacement and concomitant-therapy restrictions but no analysis set.
The analysis attachment specifies models without an operational ITT or efficacy population.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as change from baseline in BPI-SF3 worst shoulder pain and resolve the confirmatory timepoint: the protocol collects it repeatedly and defines response at end of treatment and trial conclusion, while the analysis attachment powers a between-group difference at Week 28 but discusses effects at end of treatment and follow-up.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies BPI-SF3 as primary and schedules assessments from baseline through Week 28.
The attachment discusses end-of-treatment and follow-up trajectories and uses a Week-28 difference for power.

requirement: Derive BPI-SF3 from the participant's worst pain during the prior seven days on the 0-to-10 scale, with lower values favorable, and define change consistently as postbaseline minus baseline so that negative change represents pain reduction.

evidence.text: The protocol defines BPI-SF3 wording, recall period and anchors.
The attachment expresses efficacy as reduction from baseline in BPI-SF3.

requirement: Define a pain responder as having at least a 30% BPI-SF3 reduction from baseline, derive responder status separately at Week 4 end of treatment and Week 28 trial conclusion, and state the denominator and rule for missing BPI-SF3.

evidence.text: The protocol defines successful pain relief as at least 30% reduction and calls for response at end of treatment and trial conclusion.

requirement: For Aim 1, estimate the pain-reduction contrast between PNS plus sham PT and sham PNS plus active PT rather than collapsing the three groups into generic PNS and PT categories.

evidence.text: Aim 1 compares PNS with PT and the randomized arms identify the corresponding single-active-treatment groups.
The attachment expects greater reduction for PNS plus sham PT than PT plus sham PNS.

requirement: For Aim 2, estimate all prespecified comparisons needed to assess the ordered expectation that PNS plus PT has the greatest pain reduction, followed by PNS plus sham PT and then sham PNS plus PT; do not replace these estimates with only an omnibus test.

evidence.text: Protocol Aim 2 states the ordered three-group efficacy hypothesis.
The attachment repeats the ordered expectation and applies the Aim 1 approach to continuous outcomes.

requirement: Operationalize the longitudinal linear mixed-effects model for each continuous outcome with treatment, time and treatment-by-time effects, and prespecify participant-level random effects, residual covariance, estimation method, denominator degrees of freedom, visit coding, baseline handling and any confounders before outcome inspection.

evidence.text: The attachment names a linear mixed-effects approach and treatment, time and interaction estimates but omits an executable correlation and estimation specification.

requirement: Prespecify the multisite strategy: assess demographic comparability and treatment-by-site interaction as planned, define a quantitative poolability criterion, and state whether site is a fixed effect, random effect, stratification factor or sensitivity analysis without selecting the approach from observed treatment results.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies three sites and includes site in adaptive allocation.
The attachment says poolability, demographic comparability and treatment-by-site interaction will be evaluated but gives no decision rule.

requirement: Define the primary estimand, including the randomized population, three assigned treatment conditions, BPI-SF3 change and confirmatory timepoint, population-level contrast, and strategies for treatment discontinuation, nonadherence, lead replacement, rescue analgesics and nonstudy shoulder therapy.

evidence.text: The protocol supplies treatment, outcome and postrandomization-event context but no complete estimand.
The attachment specifies longitudinal comparisons without intercurrent-event strategies.

requirement: Resolve the ambiguous type-I-error statement before analysis: define whether the one-sided alpha 0.05 described as combined applies across all three pairwise comparisons, give the allocation or gatekeeping rule across Aims 1 and 2 and timepoints, and align confidence intervals and success decisions with that rule.

evidence.text: The power paragraph cites alpha 0.05 combined and a one-sided equal-variance t test of three pairwise comparisons without an executable multiplicity rule.

requirement: Specify the primary missing-data assumption and model-based handling of incomplete repeated BPI-SF3 values, distinguish intermittent missing visits from dropout, report observed-data counts by arm and visit, and define at least one clinically interpretable sensitivity analysis for departures from MAR.

evidence.text: The attachment says mixed models accommodate missing data and dropouts but does not state an assumption or sensitivity analysis.

requirement: Analyze the binary 30% pain-responder outcome with logistic regression using treatment group as the exposure, and prespecify the reference group, visit-specific or repeated-response structure, covariates, odds or risk effect scale, confidence intervals and handling of missing response status.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the 30% responder outcome.
The attachment specifies logistic regression with treatment group as independent variable but no further implementation details.

requirement: Keep secondary clinical outcomes secondary and define their derivations and visits, including BPI-SF9 pain interference as the mean of seven 0-to-10 domains, SF-36 quality of life, shoulder-abduction torque, shoulder kinematics and optional upper-limb Fugl-Meyer score.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies the secondary outcomes and provides BPI-SF9 and mechanistic measurement rules.

requirement: Treat Aim 3 mechanism analyses as exploratory and prespecify how changes in mechanical pain threshold, optional pinprick threshold, temporal summation or wind-up ratio and biomechanical measures will be associated with PNS and PT exposure without confirmatory causal claims.

evidence.text: The protocol labels Aim 3 exploratory and defines the central-sensitization and biomechanical measurements.

requirement: Document the power calculation as detecting a 2.0-point Week-28 BPI-SF3 difference with assumed SD 2.4, 80% power, a one-sided equal-variance two-sample t-test and 27 participants per group before dropout inflation, while flagging the undefined meaning of combined alpha and the assumed ordering across three groups.

evidence.text: The attachment provides the effect, SD, power, test, group size and ordering assumptions but labels alpha only as 0.05 combined.

requirement: Define a safety population based on actual exposure and summarize adverse events by randomized and received treatment, participant incidence, event count, severity, seriousness and relationship, with separate reporting of lead-site infection or irritation, retained electrode fragments and treatment discontinuations.

evidence.text: The protocol describes lead-specific risks, repeated AE collection, quarterly review and six-month DSMB monitoring but does not give statistical safety-set or summary rules.

requirement: Before release, confirm from source history that the protocol export and analysis attachment dated 2021-11-05 are an unmodified prospective governing pair: they postdate the 2017 study start but predate 2024 primary completion and use prospective language, and the study must be excluded if outcome-informed revision or attachment drift is found.

evidence.text: The export cover is dated 2021-11-05 and its IRB body records an anticipated start and end while the registry chronology places it during enrollment.
The separately uploaded attachment shares the title, NCT and date and uses anticipated and future-tense analysis language, without results.

requirement: Keep the two-page reference analysis attachment annotation-only: the model-visible 79-page protocol may provide study design, outcomes, adaptive randomization and prospective target, but the reference's power test, linear mixed-effects model, site checks and logistic responder model must not be exposed as protocol-only input.

evidence.text: Full-text comparison found no copy of the reference's power, mixed-model, site-poolability or logistic-regression language in the protocol export.
The independent analysis attachment contains the target statistical decisions and remains under the reference role.
